package: "openpipeline"
version: "v4.2.0"
title: "consensus_vote"
subtitle: "openpipeline v4.2.0"
toc: true
namespace: "Annotate"
description: "Combines cell type predictions from multiple annotation methods into a single consensus prediction using a weighted majority vote. For each cell, each method votes for its predicted cell type, optionally weighted by the probability score and/or a per-method weight. The consensus prediction is the cell type with the highest total weighted vote. Note that this method does not leverage pre-existing ontology or perform any reconciliation of cell type labels across methods, so the same cell type may be represented by different labels in different methods and will be treated as distinct cell types in the vote."
type: "module"
latest: "true"

For each cell, each method votes for its predicted cell type, optionally weighted by the probability score and/or a per-method weight. The consensus prediction is the cell type with the highest total weighted vote. Note that this method does not leverage pre-existing ontology or perform any reconciliation of cell type labels across methods, so the same cell type may be represented by different labels in different methods and will be treated as distinct cell types in the vote

`--input_obs_predictions`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
One or more .obs column names containing cell type predictions (labels) from
different annotation methods.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string` [required]{.arg-required}

[Example]{.arg-key} `"scanvi_pred"`, `"celltypist_pred"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--input_obs_probabilities`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
One or more .obs column names containing prediction probability scores,
one per method in --input_obs_predictions. When provided, each method's
vote is scaled by the probability score for that cell (in addition to
any per-method --weights). Must be the same length as --input_obs_predictions.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"scanvi_prob"`, `"celltypist_prob"`, `"singler_prob"`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--tie_label`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Label to assign when two or more cell types receive equal votes.
If not provided, tied cells are assigned None (missing value).
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"Unknown"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--weights`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Per-method weights for the consensus vote. Must be the same length as
--input_obs_predictions when provided. Weights are normalized to sum to 1
before use. If not provided, all methods are weighted equally.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
List of `double`

[Example]{.arg-key} `1.0`, `2.0`

[Separator]{.arg-key} `";"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/annotate/consensus_vote/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/annotate/consensus_vote);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/annotate/consensus_vote/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
